[Pre-reflection] The strategy's reliance on multiple overlapping conditions (Bollinger cross, RSI filter, ATR risk management) may lead to overfitting and reduced robustness in varying market regimes. The exit rules are too broad and could trigger premature exits during strong trends, reducing profitability. The hybrid approach may dilute the effectiveness of individual components, especially in trending vs. mean-reverting environments.
[Backup plan] If results are poor, I'd simplify to a pure momentum + ATR stop-loss approach with fixed time-based exits. If Sharpe is low, I'd optimize RSI threshold and ATR multiplier parameters. As an alternative, I'd test a breakout strategy with volatility-adjusted entry filters using only Bollinger and ATR, eliminating RSI to reduce complexity and potential noise.

[Pre-reflection] The strategy's reliance on multiple indicators without proper optimization may lead to overfitting and false signals. The exit rule based on ADX below 20 is too simplistic and may cause premature exits during trending markets. High volatility (82%) and negative Sharpe (-20) suggest poor risk management and inconsistent entry timing.
[Backup plan] If results are poor, try adding a volatility filter (e.g., ATR-based position sizing) or switching to a momentum-based entry (e.g., RSI above 60 with ADX > 25). If Sharpe is low, adjust Bollinger band length (e.g., 20-day) and RSI period (e.g., 14-day) to reduce whipsaws. As alternative, consider a breakout strategy with dynamic stop-losses or a mean reversion approach using z-scores instead of fixed thresholds.
